schemes.official_name: Software Engineering Project (undergraduate Computer Science client projects)
schemes.description: Second-year Computer Science undergraduates work in groups of about four to six on a software problem for a real-world client over 22 weeks (October to May), run 'as a software consultancy'. Teams use an agile method, meet the client every two to three weeks, and release a prototype/MVP, beta and final release to the client. Proposals come from companies via the Industrial Liaison Office.
schemes.admin_host: School of Computer Science / Industrial Liaison Office, Faculty of Science and Engineering
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Not evidenced beyond Computer Science undergraduates.
schemes.credit_assessment: 20 credits; 100% coursework, assessed in groups (catalogue entry carries an unreliable year label, '2036/37').
schemes.delivery_format: In-person team project with regular client meetings
schemes.project_evidence: Teams specify, design, implement and evaluate a software system with MVP, beta and final release milestones (sources 1, 2).
schemes.group_evidence: 'Each group contains approximately six students' (one page) / 'approximately four' (other pages); assessment is in groups (sources 1-3).
schemes.employer_evidence: 'Students work as a group on a problem for a real-world client'; clients propose the brief, give student effort free of charge and must meet the team every two to three weeks (sources 1, 2).
schemes.partner_role: Client supplies brief and meets team regularly for feedback; pages are addressed to companies with a 'software need'. Whether some clients are internal/academic is not stated.
schemes.deliverable: Working software prototype/system delivered to the client
schemes.unresolved: No dated 2025/26 or 2026/27 source for this unit (the only catalogue hit is labelled 2036/37, an obvious placeholder). Group size conflicts (4 vs 6). Compulsory/optional status and programme list not confirmed. A BSc Computer Science with AI 2026-entry page mentions an AI software team project for a real client with an industrial mentor; not confirmed as the same unit.

sources.title: Undergraduate software engineering projects

schemes.employer_evidence: Client submits a brief (description, motivation, constraints, IP), contributes no fee but must meet student teams every two to three weeks to review progress and steer (source 1).

schemes.english_name: Mathematical and Data Modelling 3 (Engineering Mathematics industrial modelling projects)
schemes.description: Third-year unit in which students work in groups of 4-6 on three six-week real-world modelling problems; two group projects are supplied by industrial partners and the third is a student-led project on a societal challenge. Each group has academic supervision and a teaching assistant. Companies submit problems via the Industrial Liaison Office and can expect a working prototype or concept.
schemes.admin_host: School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology
schemes.delivery_format: Group projects with academic supervision and TA
schemes.project_evidence: Students 'work in groups to solve three real-world problems, each ... a total of 6 weeks' (source 1); prototype or concept expected (source 2).
schemes.group_evidence: Groups of 4-6 students (source 1); ILO page: about 5 students per project-problem (source 2).
schemes.employer_evidence: 'Two group projects will be supplied by industrial partners' (source 1); partners propose open-ended problems via the ILO (source 2). The third project is student-led and not industry-set.
schemes.partner_role: Industrial partners supply the problems for two of the three group projects; engagement in feedback not detailed.
schemes.deliverable: Working prototype or concept/model per problem
schemes.unresolved: Compulsory/optional status, credit value and exact programmes not retrieved. Partner names not evidenced. Industrial/external share applies to 2 of 3 projects.

sources.title: Unit information: Mathematical and Data Modelling 3

schemes.official_name: Design Project (Civil Engineering) / Civil Engineering Design Projects with external clients
schemes.description: MEng capstone group design project developing a RIBA stage 1-2 design from a brief supplied by industry or by an academic. The ILO invites external clients (e.g. consultancies) to submit briefs; clients meet students at least twice a year, give feedback at a December poster session and are not involved in marking.
schemes.admin_host: School of Civil, Aerospace and Design Engineering / ILO
schemes.duration: Academic year (TB4 unit; client selection early October, poster session December)
schemes.delivery_format: Group design project with supervisor and optional industrial advisor
schemes.project_evidence: Develop a RIBA stage 2 project from a basic brief; capstone integrating prior learning (source 1).
schemes.group_evidence: ILO page: 'group projects' on real design briefs (source 2); unit assessment includes group final report (source 1).
schemes.employer_evidence: Briefs come 'from industry or from an academic' (source 1); only 'some projects have industrial advisors'; ILO page invites external client briefs and says clients meet students at least twice a year (source 2). External share not specified.
schemes.partner_role: External client proposes brief, meets students and comments at poster session; internal academic-set briefs also used.
schemes.named_partners: Arcadis pitched a Holyhead train-care facility brief to an earlier 4th-year group (blog, ~2023); no 2025/26 clients evidenced.
schemes.unresolved: Share of projects with external clients in 2025/26 not published; C therefore Unclear. ILO brief dates are undated.

profile_md:
Bristol has no university-wide, compulsory employer-project scheme; qualifying provision is distributed across schools, with the Industrial Liaison Office (Faculty of Science and Engineering) acting as the main broker of client briefs.

**Verified current routes.** Engineering Mathematics' *Mathematical and Data Modelling 3* (2026/27) puts groups of 4-6 on three six-week problems, two supplied by industrial partners. The Business School's final-year *Management Consultancy* (EFIM30064, 2025/26) places groups of 4-6 on briefs from outside organisations, mostly charities. The Business School *Micro-Internship* (200 Masters places, 3 weeks, extracurricular) assigns random teams to an industry client. The MSc Marketing applied project (small group, external commercial/third-sector partners) and the Law School's selective Human Rights Law Clinic (student-led teams researching to partner briefs, ~70 members) are also current.

**Credible but not currently evidenced.** Undergraduate Software Engineering Project and MSc Summer Team Project (client-proposed, teams of 4-6) rest on undated ILO pages; Geography's Consultancy Project (3-5 student teams, external clients) appears only in a mislabelled catalogue entry.

**Partial matches.** Civil Engineering MEng Design Project and Data Science Mini-Project use external clients only 'whenever possible' or alongside academic briefs, so C is unclear. Business Analytics, BIE and Data Science for Business routes lack group/partner detail.

Participation is mostly optional or within named programmes; only a few routes are selective. Short formats (City Challenges, one afternoon) are recorded but weak. Faculty PLN live briefs are partner-facing and not tied to identifiable credit units.
gaps: Further departmental instances likely (Aerospace/Electrical MEng industrial group design projects, Computer Science AI software team project, other MSc business projects, Veterinary/Medicine/Dentistry/Architecture community or client projects not found). Unit catalogue results often carry unreliable future year labels (2031-2038) so several units lack genuine current-year evidence. Partner names and cohort sizes mostly unpublished. Humanities/social science client-team units not found. 38 searches used; Open Unit lists not examined unit by unit.
